summary: Bell Mountain #1 and #2 lookouts are both listed as removed; the Forest Service says only concrete pilings remain at the summit.

facts.status_note: Lookout record marks both towers removed; the Forest Service says the tower is no longer there, with concrete pilings at the summit.

access.note: Summit lies in the Bell Mountain Wilderness and is reached on foot by trail. Dispersed camping is allowed; there are no structures.

visit.trail_note: No tower to climb. Trailheads on the north and southwest edges of the wilderness lead to loops across the summit.

events.note: Lookout record marks Bell Mountain #1 and #2 as removed; no date given.

evidence.supports: Location: Iron County, about 13 miles west of Irontown
evidence.quote: Located in Iron County, Missouri, approximately 13 miles west of Irontown and 17 miles east of Boss,
Elevations range from 1,702 feet at Bell Mountain

evidence.supports: Managed by Mark Twain National Forest
Concrete pilings remain at summit; tower no longer there
evidence.quote: Concrete pilings of an old fire tower are right at the top of the summit.
The tower is no longer there.

evidence.supports: Trailheads and loops across the summit
evidence.quote: Trailheads at the north and southwestern edges of the park are connected with entry and then loops crossing the mountain summit and slope

evidence.supports: Dispersed camping; no toilets or structures
evidence.quote: There are no toilets, no structures, no trash cans, no treated water, and no fire grates available.

evidence.supports: Social post claims a standing rusted steel tower
evidence.quote: rusted steel tower that still climbs above the treeline

evidence.supports: Social post claims CCC construction in the 1930s
evidence.quote: Built by Civilian Conservation Corps workers in the 1930s

sources.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
sources.publisher: Mark Twain National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A social media post says a rusted steel tower still stands; the Forest Service page says the tower is no longer there and the lookout record marks both removed. The record follows the agency page.

notes_for_editor: Brief status unknown updated to gone. No build date or builder in the reliable sources, so the story omits construction. The Instagram post (source 3) is a social media claim and is cited only to flag the conflict; it is not evidence that a tower stands. Trailhead and camping details come from the Forest Service page.
